_about: Camera pieces 9, 10, 11, 12 and 15 as film.json snippets, with the numbers used in 'Armor Where Nobody Shot'. A take is a list of STATIONS inside one place: the camera flies, lands, rests, flies again, no cut. Station keys as read by tools/film_plan.py: at = the frame the camera LANDS (put it on the word, or 2-6 f before); travel = seconds of flight before the landing; hold = seconds of rest after it; creep = slow push per frame during the rest (0 = locked off); drift = [x, y, z] metres the camera slides during the rest; via = points the flight bends through; lens in mm; lead = 0 everywhere in this film. Positions are metres in that film's world and are NOT reusable: every pos, aim and lens below is content. What is reusable is the order of stations and the travel / hold / creep numbers. Always run tools/film_plan.py check and node tools/frame_checks/check.mjs after writing stations.

09_push_in_on_named_thing.what: Inside the running take the camera pushes in on the thing the voice names (0.3-0.5 s), the thing DOES something for about 1 s, then the camera pulls back or tilts to a face.
09_push_in_on_named_thing.armor_main_example: pins stretch, 'a few SPOTS never get a pin ... all the mathematician STARES at' (film frames; build_film.py lines 76-77 show them 18 higher)

stations.subject: map_oval
stations._note: flight f505-518; the thing's own act starts 2 f AFTER the landing: the bare ovals blink 3 x 9 f from f520 (pin_fire.oval_blink)

stations.subject: mathematician_bare
stations._note: pull back to the face that reacts (he stares, dead still); the realisation move starts at f576

other_armor_uses: S4 f312 the barrel on 'trash': wide station at f297 (hold 0.17), then travel 0.33, hold 0.75, creep 0.003; the lid lifts f304 and the flies burst f306, so the camera DIVES WITH the lid; out to the Chief at f343 in 0.27 s
S1 f96 the clean cowl: travel 1.1 (it has to fly round the man, via one point), lens 40, hold 1.05, creep 0.0015; the two taps at f108 and f117 are the thing's act; kicks 0.3 and 0.4 on the taps
S4 f213 the shelf: lens 50, travel 0.33, hold 0.5
rules: the thing must DO something during the rest (a blink, a tap, a hit, a hand placing it); a rest over 1.5 s needs a new event about every second
a hand, tool or face is in the close frame; light and place are the wide's
creep 0.0015-0.003 keeps a rest alive; 0 only when things in frame move a lot
after the rest go to a FACE, not to the next thing, unless the story is a list
09_push_in_on_named_thing.must_change: the thing and what it does on its word; the direction of the push (from where the character looks at it); how close (the thing at least a third of frame height, or small but marked); the face it returns to and what that face feels

10_low_angle_closeup_on_a_mark_being_mad.what: The camera comes down LOW first, then rises and pushes in with a long lens onto the spot where a hand makes a mark, looking up; the maker's arm, tool and face stay in the picture; the rest lasts as long as the stroke.
10_low_angle_closeup_on_a_mark_being_mad.armor_example: S1 'has just CHALKED A CIRCLE' (build_film.py lines 71-72 and 82-85; CB: 'from down below camera move')

stations.subject: chief
stations._note: camera 0.12 m off the ground, wide lens, looking up at the man and the mark; almost no rest: it is a turning point of the flight

stations.subject: last_ring
stations._note: rise to 0.55 m and push in; the closeness comes from the LENS (19 to 68 mm), not from moving nearer, so the character's hand stays in reach on his card. The stroke runs f154-195: the camera is still arriving while the line grows and lands for its closing

stations.subject: chief
stations._note: pull back WITH his proud step to all the marks and all the people whole in frame

rules: measure where the mark's points land on the character's card before fixing the camera height: in the armor film a lens at 0.75 m put the ring 114-199 px above the card's zero line, at 1.02 m 143-239 px, and above about 205 px the kit cuts the drawing
the mark must be large enough to read on a phone at the moment its word is said
use with moves/stroke_drawn_live.mjs: one hand_at point per frame
10_low_angle_closeup_on_a_mark_being_mad.must_change: the mark, the surface (overhead here; a wall or a table changes the angle: the piece is 'from the side the mark is NOT hidden by the hand'), the lens pair, and what the wide after it reveals

11_fly_through_an_object_to_change_place.what: The take ends by flying INTO a small dark or glowing opening of a real object until it fills the lens; the next place opens out of the same kind of opening. The only way two places join, besides an 8-12 f blend.

out_of_S1.subject: hole
out_of_S1._note: pos = the hole's centre + 0.62 m along its outward normal; aim = 1.2 m beyond the hole on the inside: the camera stops just short and looks through (build_film.py lines 16, 74, 90-91). Hole radius 0.12 m. The last 13 frames (f343-355) are the join and were never re-rendered in fix rounds: patch_cam.py re-timed f332-342 onto the old path instead

into_S2.subject: holes
into_S2._note: the next stretch starts INSIDE the body looking out through the holes, already drifting, so the motion carries over

into.subject: lantern
into._note: 0.24 m behind the lantern in his raised fist, looking through its glow

out.subject: stove
out._note: 0.24 m from the same lantern standing on the stove in the other place; the pull back starts at once

rules: the object is part of the story at that moment (the hole the film is about; the lantern he carries), never a convenient door
both sides are filled by the same colour and brightness on the join frame
the join frames are frozen once two stretches are rendered: a later fix re-times the frames before them, never the join
a set shader that the lens enters must guard pow, sqrt and divisions or the graphics card draws black (CB_RULES section 10)
11_fly_through_an_object_to_change_place.must_change: the object and why this story passes through it; which way the next place opens (out of the same object, or its twin); the travel time into it (0.2 s for a hand-held lantern, 0.9 s for a flight across a wing)

12_fly_land_rest.what: How a whole stretch is written: ONE take, 6-17 stations; each station is a flight that lands on a word and a rest in which the acting happens.

numbers_from_the_armor_film.stations_per_stretch: S1 8 in 11.8 s; pins 15 in 21 s; S4 16 in two takes
numbers_from_the_armor_film.travel_s: 0.17-1.37; a push-in 0.33-0.5; a pull back 0.5-0.8; a flight across the set 0.9-1.4
numbers_from_the_armor_film.hold_s: a rest with acting 0.9-2.5; a rest on a thing 0.5-1.05; a pass-through point 0.03-0.07 (the camera only turns there)
numbers_from_the_armor_film.creep: 0.0006-0.004 per frame on rests; 0 on pass-through points and on the last station of a take
numbers_from_the_armor_film.drift_m: 0.03-0.1 on long rests (a slow slide sideways)
numbers_from_the_armor_film.lens_mm: 24 by default; 14-19 for a low wide; 40-68 for a close on a small thing; 55-60 through a far door
numbers_from_the_armor_film.kicks: film.json kicks [{at, amp}]: 0.3-0.5 on a tap or a burst, 0.8 on a slap, 1.0 on a heavy clang

12_fly_land_rest.example_take: episodes/armor-no-holes/stretches/armor-s1-hook/build_film.py lines 75-93 (8 stations with the purpose of each written out)
rules: a station's `at` is a plain frame number from words.json, never shifted by a tool
frame 0 is the approved script's FRAME 0 picture: hold 0.2 s, then fly
no stop on a wide just to show the wide: fix round 3 of S1 removed it and made one flight f6-46
check every frame of every rest for a figure cut by the frame edge (node tools/frame_checks/check.mjs)
floor at most a third of a wide
12_fly_land_rest.must_change: everything spatial. Keep only: flight short, rest on the word, something happens in every rest, the camera idea of the film named once (camera_idea in film.json)

15_the_hundreds_count_closeup.what: 'Many of one thing': the camera lands close ON the surface while the things are still arriving, so the count is seen growing: heads fill the frame, every hit flashes, the surface shudders, a light band runs over them, a small counter races; then ONE pull back shows the whole.
15_the_hundreds_count_closeup.armor_example: pins stretch 'By Friday there are HUNDREDS' (film frames; build_film.py lines 73-74, 59-60, 167)

stations.subject: pins
stations._note: 0.78 m from the paper, square on; drift along the row instead of creep

stations.subject: drawing
stations._note: the pull back runs WHILE the storm still lands (the last storm hits land at about f390 in film frames) and ends on the full sheet

with.storm: fx/fly_and_hit.js group {kind: 'storm', f0: 335, f1: 388, waves: 3} in film frames: about 300 things in 1.8 s
with.flash: pin_fire.flash 0.075 m: each head lights up gold on its hit and dies over 8 f
with.light_band: fx/highlight_part.js pinsCloseUp: two sweeps f352-363 and f366-377, band 0.42
with.counter: a small counter plate ON the sheet inside the close frame (pin_fire.counter2, shown f40-566), digits = fly_and_hit.countIn
with.head_size: pin_fire.head_k 1.8: a head is about 20 px at the wide rest

15_the_hundreds_count_closeup.reference: CLOSEUP_STUDY.md section 6: the reference channel reveals 'many of one thing' in under half a second with a hand placing the newest. The armor version has NO hand in the close frame; that is its weak point (see INDEX.md).
15_the_hundreds_count_closeup.must_change: the thing counted and what makes its number believable in THIS story (a counter, a tally, a ruler beside them, a stack that grows past something of known size); the surface; whether a hand places the newest; the word the landing sits on
